title: Privilege change chronicle and actor/target model for RBAC v2 audit
creator: Maya Singh
description: Define a practical, storage-efficient event envelope and a compact differential format for privilege and admin events in the RBAC v2 rollout. Focus: what to log (intent vs state), canonical actor/target model with SSO/SAML linkage, delta encoding for config changes, redaction/hashing rules, and operational lookup paths for investigations.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical event envelope is documented and approved by Security and Compliance
A compact change format (CCC) is specified with parsing rules and validation tests
Actor mapping from SSO/SAML assertions to internal principal IDs is specified including confidence scoring
Storage schema draft for ledger table and indices is defined, with retention and redaction policy
E2E example events (privilege grant, role-binding update, SAML-linked login) are provided and pass schema validation tooling
technical_notes: We propose a two-tier envelope: 1) Envelope metadata (flat indexed fields) for fast queries: event_id, occurred_at, event_type, actor_principal_id, actor_kind, target_kind, target_id, classification_tags. 2) Payload_blob: a compact, base64-encoded CCC delta plus optional clear-text human summary. CCC (Compact Change Chronicle) uses newline-separated op records with short op codes: U (update), A (add), R (remove), L (link). Each op: <OP>|<path>|<before_hex>|<after_hex>. Hex encoding reduces JSON verbosity and keeps blobs compact for large structs. Example op: U|/bindings/role:abc|2f616c676f6e|2f616c676f6e2f6164646564. Sensitive string fields are hashed and salted (HMAC-SHA256) with KMS-backed key before storage. Full text copies of diff are stored only for retention_class = sensitive-high. Non-sensitive changes get only CCC.
delta_format_spec:
CCC (Compact Change Chronicle) grammar: lines separated by 
. Fields separated by |. Ops: A (add), U (update), R (remove), M (move), L (link). Path: JSON Pointer-like but flattened (no spaces). Values encoded: if simple primitive -> hex UTF-8; if structured -> gzip+base64. The parser must be idempotent and tolerant of unknown ops. To reconstruct before/after state, apply ops in chronological order. For large config blobs we store a precomputed content-hash to allow compact checksums instead of full content in long-term storage.
actor_model: Actors are normalised to a union of: internal_user, external_identity (SSO provider), service_principal, system_agent. Canonical actor fields: principal_id (internal), actor_kind, provider (eg 'okta', 'saml:acme-idp'), external_subject (opaque), actor_confidence (0..100). For SAML: we record assertion_id, assertion_issued_at, and a mapping_trace which is a deterministic HMAC mapping from external_subject to canonical principal_id (HMAC key in KMS). Actor_confidence = weighted score of (assertion_freshness, identity_link_age, session_auth_strength).
target_model: Targets include organizational objects: team, project, role, binding, resource, key. Each target recorded with target_kind, target_id (opaque), human_summary, prior_state_snapshot_ref (content-hash or small embedded JSON if <= 2KB). For role/binding updates we include a short canonical semantics tag: grant|revoke|modify|escalate. For membership churn events we also capture membership_delta_count as integer in the envelope for quick aggregation.
redaction_and_privacy: PII (email, phone, raw SAML assertions) must be redacted at ingestion unless retention_class=investigation and explicit approval exists. Redaction strategy: replace with deterministic HMAC token and keep a separate sealed lookup table accessible only via recovery process requiring 2-step approval. For log exports, remove all external_subject values and replace with actor_confidence buckets.
retention_and_sampling: Retention classes: sensitive-high (admin privilege grants, RBAC policy changes) kept full for 7 years; medium (role-binding changes, delegation) kept 365 days full, then compacted to summary aggregates for 2 additional years; low (informational view events) kept 90 days. Sampling: for high volume identity events (SAML logins) store full events for 1 in 10 by default plus all anomalous (confidence < 40) and admin-session events. Sampling flags must be encoded in envelope to allow reconstructing counts.
storage_and_indices: Ledger table (append-only) columns: event_id (PK), occurred_at, event_type, actor_principal_id, actor_kind, target_kind, target_id, classification_tags (array), actor_confidence, retention_class, payload_blob (CCC), envelope_summary (text). Indices: (actor_principal_id, occurred_at), (target_kind, target_id, occurred_at), (event_type, occurred_at). Offer a denormalized lookup index for SSO assertion_id -> event_id to speed investigations.
lookup_and_investigation_paths: Common queries: timeline for actor_principal_id, timeline for target_id, PKCS-style provenance chain (follow change blobs using prior_state_snapshot_ref), SAML assertion audit lookup by assertion_id, and aggregated counts per role change type. Expose a small investigation API that returns envelope_summary plus links to full payload for authorized auditors.
backfill_strategy: Backfill existing RBAC-related events by ingesting from legacy audit logs into CCC via a migration script. Migrate in two phases: 1) ingest high-sensitivity events only and validate schema mapping; 2) bulk ingest rest with dedup checks using content-hash. Keep migration idempotent and produce mapping table legacy_event_id -> new_event_id.
migration_steps: Write CCC encoder/decoder in Python and Go (libraries) and unit tests
Prototype ingestion pipeline that validates and computes actor_confidence and principal mapping
Deploy storage schema to staging with indices and run a 7-day retention smoke test
Backfill high-sensitivity legacy events and run investigative queries to validate retrieval latency
Security review and redaction verification, then enable in prod behind feature flag
rollout_plan: Phase 0: spec review and security sign-off (3 sprints). Phase 1: library + staging storage (2 sprints). Phase 2: pilot with RBAC v2 control plane (1 sprint) capturing role-binding updates. Phase 3: enable for all admin flows and schedule retention compaction jobs. Feature flag gating required for each phase. Provide break-glass rollback path that stops writing to new ledger and continues writing to legacy log for 48 hours.
monitoring_and_alerting: Track: write failure rate to ledger, average payload_blob size, percent of events marked sensitive-high, actor mapping failures (unmapped external_subjects), and CCC parse error rate. Alert thresholds: mapping_failures > 0.5% over 30m; parse errors > 0.1% over 30m.
open_questions: Do we require full-text storage of diffs for all sensitive-high events or can we rely on compact hashes with retrieval on-demand?
Should actor_confidence be computed synchronously at ingestion or via async enrichment?
Do we keep a reversible mapping for external_subject -> principal_id in prod or make it recoverable only via sealed key access?
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose CCC over JSON-Patch for storage efficiency and consistent gzip+base64 strategy agreed
2026-03-04: Decide to HMAC external_subject with KMS key rather than store cleartext SAML assertion ids
2026-03-09: Retention policy draft approved by Compliance for sensitive-high 7 years
